summary: Apply ISA/IEC 62443, OT risk controls, and incident response across energy assets. Build practical resilience outputs. Enquire about delivery.
lede: Cybersecurity training for oil and energy operations helps OT, plant, safety, and risk professionals protect industrial systems while considering operational consequences. Participants practise inventorying assets, assessing cyber-physical risks, and planning controls that account for legacy equipment and vendor access. They also develop zone-and-conduit designs, incident response playbooks, and resilience reporting to support safer, more reliable operations.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who make or influence cybersecurity, safety, reliability, and risk decisions in energy operations. It suits intermediate practitioners who can relate control requirements to real assets and operating constraints, while remaining accessible to experienced managers who need a structured OT security operating model.
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to energy operations, industrial control systems, information security, process safety, HSE, or operational risk. Familiarity with basic networking, asset registers, incident reporting, and risk matrices will help, but you do not need programming experience or prior ISA/IEC 62443 certification. Coding is not required for completion. AI-assisted anomaly analysis and digital monitoring appear at operational application and governance level, while ISA/IEC 62443 architecture, risk assessment, and incident response receive hands-on design treatment.
